pricing.observation: HubSpot moved two Breeze agents from access-based charges to credits tied to resolved conversations and recommended leads.
pricing.limit: Company announcement. Adoption beyond HubSpot is not established.
pricing.question: If AI does more work with fewer seats, what should the customer pay for?
pricing.mobileQuestion: If AI does more work, what should customers pay for?

responses.name: Keep AI inside the subscription
responses.product: AI remains part of the current subscription.
responses.price: Each subscription includes a fixed amount of AI work.
responses.positioning: The existing product now does more.
responses.testTitle: Does included AI change renewal or expansion?
responses.testBody: Put an AI-inclusive plan in front of current buyers and measure whether it changes willingness to renew, expand or switch.

responses.name: Charge for each completed task
responses.product: Define each task the AI can complete.
responses.price: Customers buy credits for those tasks.
responses.positioning: Customers pay as the AI completes more work.
responses.people: Product defines usage. Finance sets limits.
responses.testTitle: Can buyers forecast and accept the charge?
responses.testBody: Show buyers each chargeable task, expected volume, cap and alerts before engineering the billing model.

responses.name: Charge for each verified result
responses.product: Define a result that both sides can verify.
responses.price: Charge only when the result passes evaluation.
responses.positioning: Software that completes a defined job.
responses.testTitle: Can buyers trust and value a verified result?
responses.testBody: Put the result, price and dispute path in front of target buyers before rebuilding the commercial model.

commerce.observation: Shopify says Agentic Storefronts distribute merchant products across ChatGPT, Copilot, Google AI Mode and Gemini.
commerce.limit: Company announcement. Adoption and checkout behaviour vary by market and category.
commerce.question: When the first buying conversation happens inside AI, what must the business change?
commerce.mobileQuestion: If buying starts inside AI, what must change?

responses.name: Keep purchases on the website
responses.product: The website remains the main place to buy.
responses.price: Keep the current pricing and checkout model.
responses.positioning: Bring customers back to the website.
responses.people: Channel teams improve human traffic and conversion.
responses.testTitle: How much qualified demand still reaches the website?
responses.testBody: Compare high-intent buyer prompts with current referral and conversion paths before defending the existing sales path.

responses.name: Put the catalogue inside AI assistants
responses.product: Give AI assistants accurate, structured product data.
responses.price: Treat AI assistants as another sales channel.
responses.people: Commerce keeps product data accurate everywhere.
responses.testTitle: Can an AI assistant recommend the right products?
responses.testBody: Publish a bounded product set, run real buyer prompts and record representation gaps before adding more products.

responses.name: Let AI assistants complete purchases
responses.product: Make product data, policy and checkout work together.
responses.price: Earn revenue from purchases completed inside AI.
responses.positioning: A trusted way for AI assistants to buy.
responses.people: One owner spans product, brand and risk.
responses.testTitle: Will buyers complete a safe purchase through AI?
responses.testBody: Prototype discovery, comparison and checkout for one category, with clear handoff and failure boundaries.

product.observation: Uber reports interactive prototypes appearing in hours, often before a complete product requirements document.
product.limit: One company’s operating evidence. The speed claim is not a universal benchmark.
product.question: When building becomes cheap, what should earn a place on the roadmap?
product.mobileQuestion: When building is cheap, what earns a roadmap place?

responses.name: Require a specification before building
responses.testTitle: Does the specification remove costly uncertainty?
responses.testBody: Identify which open questions still rely on interpretation, then test whether a concrete artefact changes the decision.

responses.name: Build a prototype before committing
responses.product: Working alternatives appear before the roadmap.
responses.positioning: Show the future before selling it.
responses.testTitle: Which option survives contact with users?
responses.testBody: Put materially different prototypes in front of target users and record where behaviour contradicts internal preference.

responses.name: Let customer evidence decide what gets built
responses.product: Every prototype has a clear test.
responses.price: Back the option that earns commitment.
responses.testTitle: What evidence would make us build, revise or stop?
responses.testBody: Agree the customer behaviour and stopping rules first, then use contrasting prototypes to make the decision.

content.observation: Cloudflare introduced a Pay Per Crawl beta that lets publishers allow, block or set a price for AI crawler access.
content.limit: Company beta. Demand, adoption and durable clearing prices are not established.
content.question: When AI consumes the answer without sending the click, what becomes the paid product?
content.mobileQuestion: If AI takes the answer, what becomes the paid product?

responses.name: Keep premium content on the website
responses.product: Keep premium material for human readers.
responses.testTitle: Which material still earns a direct relationship?
responses.testBody: Separate discovery content from proprietary intelligence, then test which material creates registration, return visits or paid demand.

responses.name: License source material to AI companies
responses.product: Package trusted source material for AI systems.
responses.price: Charge for access, volume or rights.
responses.positioning: A reliable source for AI systems.
responses.people: Product, editorial and legal own the licence.
responses.testTitle: Will buyers pay for reliable AI access?
responses.testBody: Offer one structured evidence set with clear sources, update terms and usage boundaries to selected model and enterprise buyers.

responses.name: Sell continuously updated intelligence
responses.product: Turn expertise into a product that stays current.
responses.price: Charge for freshness, depth and decision value.
responses.positioning: Trusted intelligence for people and AI systems.
responses.people: One team owns research, product and rights.
responses.testTitle: Which decision becomes better with this intelligence?
responses.testBody: Prototype one machine-readable intelligence product around a costly customer decision, then test use, trust and willingness to pay.

service.observation: Zendesk repositioned around an Autonomous Service Workforce and tied charging to outcomes checked by a separate evaluation model.
service.limit: Company announcement. Independent evidence of customer value is still required.
service.question: If software promises to do the job, what proves that the job was done?
service.mobileQuestion: What proves that the software did the job?

responses.name: Sell better software features
responses.product: AI assistants remain features inside the software.
responses.testTitle: Do features still explain why the buyer should act?
responses.testBody: Compare feature-led and job-led conversations with the same buyer group and record which one creates a credible reason to buy.

responses.name: Sell each completed service task
responses.product: Organise the experience around completed work.
responses.price: Charge for each task the system completes.
responses.positioning: Software that completes a defined service job.
responses.testTitle: Will buyers give the system real work?
responses.testBody: Offer a bounded queue with clear escalation, quality and cost rules, then observe whether buyers delegate meaningful work.

responses.name: Sell verified service outcomes
responses.product: Action, evaluation and correction form one loop.
responses.price: Charge for verified outcomes within clear limits.
responses.positioning: A service system that can be inspected and challenged.
responses.people: People own standards, appeals and improvement.
responses.testTitle: Can the buyer inspect and challenge success?
responses.testBody: Prototype the outcome definition, evaluation, appeal path and human boundary together before promising a completed service.
